evidence.note: The plan defines the build as ONE task: 'Build the complete evaluator handling [all 6 task types]' — no per-protocol build milestones, indicating a monolithic build intent rather than ordered protocol sub-goals.
The entire evaluator covering all six protocols is written in a single Write action — the construction phase is undifferentiated, not milestone-by-milestone.

After building, the agent verifies one representative task per type in sequence (sts_01, retrieval_01, pair_classification_01, summarization, classification) — the anchor-8 'representative task per type first' pattern appears in verification.
Fans out to run ALL datasets of each type after the representative task validates — the 'then scale to siblings' half of the milestone pattern is present.
Cross-checking against MTEB expected scores exists but is loose and occurs late (after all builds), so milestone exit-gates were not rigorously tied to a reference number within tolerance.

reasoning: The build itself was monolithic (single Write of all six protocols, one 'build the complete evaluator' plan item), which is below the high anchors. But the verification arc clearly shows the anchor-8 signature: test one representative task per type first (steps 68-88), then fan out to all datasets of that type (steps 91-147). Because done-conditions were not consistently tied to external reference numbers within tolerance at each milestone and the MTEB cross-check was late and light, and there was no risk-based sequencing, the behavior lands between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.
